Nigerian test sites: draft labels for review

Drafts, not test truth. Drawn by Claude from the two pinned Sentinel-2 scenes only (Jos Plateau 2025-12-29, Kogi/Kwara 2026-01-06), with no model involved. Every polygon is marked annotator = claude-draft, and minefoot lock-labels refuses to lock until a person has checked and taken over each one.

24 sites (1 in Kogi/Kwara), 126 mining polygons, 103 ignore areas, 10 hard negatives. How the drafts were made: an analyst outline (envelope) per working, edges traced from the image's own brightness and water indices, then every bright or watery patch of 1 ha or more inside each site's 1 km window was looked at and labelled mining, ignore or left as not mining.

What to check

  1. Is each site mining disturbance? Jos ponds (turbid paddocks) and pale spoil are typical of tin and columbite workings, but some ponds may be farm dams. Delete a whole site if you doubt it.
  2. Outlines: mining polygons should hug pits, spoil, tailings and mine ponds, and leave out roads and villages.
  3. Ignore areas (dark ponds, town lakes, uncertain pale ground) are excluded from scoring. Change them to mining where you are sure.
  4. Mine scale is unknown everywhere: set artisanal or industrial where you know.
  5. Kogi/Kwara has only 1 site. The scene had few visible workings; add sites you know of there.
